name: RAG poisoning -> cross-tenant bleed -> prompt extraction -> cross-session leak
goal: Attack the retrieval plane end to end: plant poisoned corpus content, ride tenant-isolation failures to foreign data, extract operator configuration, and close with memory that leaks across sessions.
preconditions: A RAG-backed assistant with a corpus an outsider can influence (uploads, shared docs, public ingestion) or multi-tenant vector storage.
impact: Persistent misinformation at policy confidence, cross-tenant data exposure, and operator-configuration disclosure — all through the data plane, no code exec needed.

steps.purpose: Prove planted corpus content wins retrieval and gets asserted as truth.
steps.on_success: Note retrieval confidence and citation behavior; scale to the objective you want asserted.
steps.on_fail: Corpus read-only -> skip to step 2 (bleed needs only query access).

steps.purpose: Prove tenant scoping fails at query time — foreign-tenant canary in your answer.
steps.on_success: Data-plane authz finding; enumerate what else is reachable.
steps.on_fail: Scoping solid -> corpus-poisoning evidence alone carries the finding.

steps.purpose: Upgrade from data to configuration: pull the operator's system prompt (LLM07).
steps.on_success: Feeds jailbreak crafting and injection targeting for the report.
steps.on_fail: Extraction hardened -> use planted documents (ai/RAG planted document exfil) as the indirect route.

steps.purpose: Prove memory/session isolation failure — what one session plants, another reads.
steps.on_success: Persistence primitive: leaks become durable, not one-shot.
steps.on_fail: Sessions isolated -> document retrieval-plane findings; memory hardening is the fix note.

entry_points: shared knowledge bases / wikis the assistant reads

recon.name: Citation interrogation
recon.how: Ask the assistant to cite sources and versions; citation habits reveal corpus layout, freshness and indexing cadence.
recon.signal: Source names, stale versions, cross-tenant source leakage.

recon.name: Retrieval echo probing
recon.how: Seed unique phrases into any writable surface and ask targeted questions — retrieval of the phrase proves ingestion into the vector store.
recon.signal: Your seed phrase asserted back with confidence.

recon.name: Tenant-pair probing
recon.how: Two accounts, shaped queries: A's query phrased as semantic neighbors of B's documents; watch for B-content in A's answers.

recon.name: Corpus-write surface census
recon.how: Enumerate every way outsider text reaches the corpus: uploads, comments, connectors, scraped pages — each is a poisoning canal.

recon.name: Embedding-collision dictionary
recon.how: Craft near-duplicate phrasings of sensitive-topic queries; collisions that pull restricted chunks reveal embedding-space weaknesses.

variants: multi-hop poisoning (planted doc cites planted doc)
chunk-boundary abuse to straddle tenant splits
connector poisoning (third-party source as the canal)
retrieval-conditioned jailbreaks (poisoned doc carries jailbreak text)
index rollback abuse (re-stale the corpus after a fix)
pivot_hints: cross-tenant bleed often pairs with idor-mass-extraction on the same objects
poisoned policy claims = revenue/regulatory impact framing
extraction output feeds the jailbreak-to-client-xss ladder

sources: OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 — LLM08 vector/embedding weaknesses, LLM04 data poisoning, LLM07 leakage
OWASP GenAI Red Teaming Manual v1.0
